title: A zygote-based assay to evaluate intranuclear shuttling in S. cerevisiae
author: Tartakoff

steps.title: Prepare synthetic agar plates
steps.instruction: Autoclave synthetic medium containing 2 % agar, pour the sterilized medium into Petri dishes, leave plates uncovered under a laminar flow hood for at least 1 hour at room temperature to evaporate residual liquid, then store plates (covered) for up to one week at 10 °C.

substeps.instruction: Pour the medium into Petri dishes.
Leave plates uncovered under a laminar flow hood for ≥1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: General experimental conditions
steps.instruction: Conduct all steps at room temperature or 30 °C, use synthetic media as described in the Cold Spring Harbor Manual, culture cells in shaken 24‑well plastic dishes, sediment cell cultures for 5 s at 5,000 × g in a tabletop micro‑fuge after transfer to Eppendorf tubes, and use 0.5 mL volumes for all cell incubations and washes.

substeps.instruction: Use synthetic media per Cold Spring Harbor Manual.
Grow cells in shaken 24‑well plastic dishes.
Sediment cultures for 5 s at 5,000 × g in a micro‑fuge after transferring to Eppendorf tubes.
Use 0.5 mL volumes for all incubations and washes.

steps.title: Prepare agarose pads for microscopy
steps.instruction: Add agarose to growth medium to a final concentration of 1.5 %, bring the mixture to a boil while vortexing, apply 0.3 mL of the molten agarose onto a microscope slide and immediately overlay with a second slide; the prepared slides may be stored horizontally for 1–2 days in a humid slide box in a refrigerator.

substeps.instruction: Add agarose to growth medium to 1.5 % final concentration.
Apply 0.3 mL of molten agarose to a microscope slide and overlay with a second slide.
Store slides horizontally for 1–2 days in a humid slide box in a refrigerator (pause point).

steps.title: Mount cell samples on agarose pad
steps.instruction: When the mating cross is ready for observation, gently slide off the upper slide to expose two agarose surfaces, apply 0.5–1.0 µL of cell‑pellet sample to either or both surfaces, place a No. 1 (1 mm) coverslip on top, and for time‑lapse imaging seal the coverslip with vaseline to reduce evaporation.

substeps.instruction: Remove the upper slide by gentle horizontal sliding to expose the agarose surfaces.
Apply 0.5–1.0 µL of cell pellet to one or both surfaces.
Place a No. 1 (1 mm) coverslip on top of the cells.
Seal the coverslip with vaseline for time‑lapse imaging.
